source_refs.note: The six levels of ecological organization with the Tidbit (PDF 228-230); Figure 25.1 is replaced by an original diagram.

items: Species, the unit of life: a group of organisms with similar physical and genetic characteristics that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring. The Indus river dolphin is a distinct species: Indus dolphins breed with one another but not with other dolphins.
Population: individuals of one species in the same area at the same time. All the Markhors in Chitral Gol National Park form one population; Markhors across Pakistan are the species.

Community: all the populations of different species living and interacting in an area, including plants, animals, fungi and bacteria; for example a mangrove forest in Karachi with its trees, mudskippers, crabs and shorebirds.

Ecosystem: the biotic (living) parts together with the abiotic (non-living) parts such as sunlight, soil, water and air; energy flows one way while nutrients cycle. The Thar Desert, with its snakes, blackbucks and shrubs and its heat, shifting dunes and rare rain, is an ecosystem.

Biome: a large region with a particular climate, soil and altitude and the plants and animals adapted to them; in Pakistan the coniferous forest of Murree and Swat, the desert of Thal and Thar, and freshwater biomes such as the Indus river system.

Biosphere: the highest level, the sum of all biomes, every part of the Earth where life exists, from the deepest trenches of the Arabian Sea to the highest Himalayan peaks and several kilometres into the air.

blocks.alt: Six linked hexagons. 1. Species: an Indus River dolphin. 2. Population: several Indus River dolphins in muddy water. 3. Community: a pond with dolphins, fish, reeds and a heron. 4. Ecosystem: sun, rain cloud, mountains, forest and a river basin with energy-flow and nutrient-cycling arrows. 5. Biome: a map of Pakistan with coniferous forest (Swat), desert (Thar) and riverine (Indus) zones. 6. Biosphere: the globe with atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere.
blocks.caption: Figure 25.1: Levels of ecological organization (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 25.1).
blocks.long_description: Panel texts: 1. SPECIES, Indus River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica minor), Defined by interbreeding and fertile offspring. 2. POPULATION, Indus River Dolphins, various, Same species in a defined area, e.g., Indus River. 3. COMMUNITY, Different populations interacting in one area. 4. ECOSYSTEM, Biotic Community + Abiotic Environment (e.g., Sindh River Basin), Energy Flow, Nutrient Cycling. 5. BIOME, Large regional unit defined by climate, CONIFEROUS FOREST (Swat), DESERT (Thar), RIVERINE (Indus). 6. BIOSPHERE, The entire zone of life on Earth, ATMOSPHERE, LITHOSPHERE, HYDROSPHERE, Global Ecosystem. Arrows lead from 1 to 6 in order.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: The biosphere is often called the 'global ecosystem': a thin envelope around the Earth where the lithosphere (land), hydrosphere (water) and atmosphere (air) interact to support life.
